vot_personal_usd_per_hr.note: USDOT BCA guidance value for local personal travel, escalated to 2024$ (Fed. column of the Caltrans matrix). Intercity personal = $28.20 (used as high). Low = previous default (unverified older guidance year). See literature/health-valuation.md and mode-choice-and-elasticities.md.

vot_business_usd_per_hr.note: Matrix row 'Truck/Business ($/hr./veh.)', USDOT value. Row label mixes truck and business travel; a pure business-traveler-per-person value was not separately verified.

walk_wait_time_multiplier.note: USDOT: walk/wait time valued at 2x (matrix: 'for wait times, the value should be doubled'). MTC TM1 uses 2x walk (<1.5 mi) and 2x initial wait (https://github.com/BayAreaMetro/travel-model-one/blob/master/model-files/model/ModeChoice.xls); SFCTA ActivitySim work-tour walk coefficient is 2.65x IVT (https://github.com/sfcta/activitysim-sfcta/blob/main/configs/resident/tour_mode_choice_coefficients.csv).

vsl_usd.note: $14.2M for a 2025 base year; $13.7M (2024), $13.2M (2023). USDOT sensitivity range is wider (unverified for 2025).

heat_walk_rr.note: All-cause mortality RR for regular walking at the reference volume (95% CI 0.83-0.96). Linear dose-response from 1.0 at 0 min.

heat_walk_ref_min_per_week.note: Reference walking volume for RR 0.89 (= 11.25 MET-h/week). Applies to ages 20-74.

heat_walk_rr_cap.note: Benefit capped at 30% risk reduction (reached at ~460 min/week). HEAT also phases benefits in over 5 years (20%/yr); we report steady state.

us_crude_mortality_20_74.note: Derived from NCHS 2023 age-specific death rates weighted by population age 20-74; population weights not verified against CDC WONDER (replace with a WONDER query). California is lower than the US average.

crash_cost_usd_per_vmt.note: Derived. Low = fatalities only (1.26 deaths/100M VMT x $13.2M). High = NHTSA ~$1.4T total societal crash cost / US VMT (unverified). Not all of this is external to the driver. See literature/health-valuation.md.

co2_kg_per_vmt.note: Typical passenger vehicle ~400 g CO2/mile. Congested low-speed SF driving emits more per mile (not modeled).

scc_usd_per_tonne.note: Central 2% discount, 2020 emissions year; range 2.5%-1.5% discount. Federal use withdrawn by Executive Order 14154 (Jan 2025); USDOT matrix shows CO2 $0 federally. Keep as a user slider. Engine uses the low bound ($120/t) of the EPA 2023 range as a conservative central value (product decision, Oct 2026).

vehicle_operating_cost_usd_per_mile.note: Derived: non-fuel auto cost $0.408/mi (matrix) + fuel at $4.37/gal (matrix, CA 2024$) / ~25 mpg (assumed) = ~$0.175/mi. Low = non-fuel only. High ~ AAA full ownership cost per mile (unverified). Marginal cost of a trip is closer to the low end.

retail_value_added_share.note: Food service VA/sales ~0.63 (derived: $703B / $1.12T). General retail is much lower (~0.25, unverified) because sales include goods cost. 0.55 is our blend for a cafe/restaurant-heavy FiDi mix (assumed weights).

sf_sales_tax_rate.note: Statewide base 7.25% (verified on CDTFA page) + SF district taxes; the 8.625% SF total is from CDTFA rate tables (unverified this session; page tables not machine-readable).

city_share_of_sales_tax.note: Bradley-Burns local 1%: 0.75% to the city/county general fund + 0.25% county transportation (split unverified this session). SF is a consolidated city-county. Low = general-fund only.

sf_property_tax_rate.note: 1% Prop 13 base + voter-approved debt ~0.16-0.18% (unverified: no SF Treasurer page could be retrieved this session; replace with the FY2025-26 secured rate).

value_of_weak_tie_usd_per_yr.note: Derived: Social Value Bank 'talks to neighbours regularly' ~GBP 4,511/person-yr divided by an assumed ~5 local weak ties, converted to USD. Upper anchor: UK DCMS severe loneliness GBP 9,537/yr (https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/963077/Loneliness_monetisation_report_V2.pdf). Wellbeing valuations are not market values; show as adjustable.

value_per_encounter_usd.note: Small value per positive chance encounter; no literature value. Sandstrom & Dunn 2014 show weak-tie interactions raise same-day wellbeing but not in $.

workdays_per_year.note: Weekdays modeled per year (52x5 minus holidays).

retail_net_new_share.note: Share of a business's revenue gain that is new to the city rather than shifted from elsewhere. Literature (Volker & Handy 2021) notes most local gains are partly redistribution; no measured value.

assessed_value_usd_per_m2.note: Assessed value of new floor area (~$465/sqft). Downtown office values have collapsed (e.g. 350 California sold ~-75%, see literature/office-to-residential-conversion.md); keep as slider.

bpr_alpha.note: BPR default. MTC Travel Model One does NOT use BPR 0.15/4: freeways use 0.20*((V/C)/0.75)^6 (~alpha 1.12, beta 6) and arterials an Akcelik curve (https://github.com/BayAreaMetro/travel-model-one/blob/master/model-files/scripts/block/SpeedFlowCurve.block). Default BPR is gentle below V/C=1; use high values as sensitivity.

lane_capacity_vph.note: TM1 regional core: freeway 2,050, expressway/ramp 1,450, major arterial 900, collector 600 (650 in CBD area type 1). Cross-check: HCM base saturation flow 1,900 pc/h/ln x g/C 0.45 = 855. secondary (800) and living_street (300) are our interpolations (assumed). See literature/congestion-modeling.md.

background_traffic_share.note: share of street traffic not modeled as agents (taxis/TNC, freight, buses, other through traffic); calibrated to counts when available

through_vehicles_per_day.note: surface through-trips crossing the area between inlets

bypass_penalty_min.note: extra minutes for a through-trip to avoid the area entirely

region_car_access.note: Which car inlets drivers from each home region can use, and the extra outside-the-map minutes of each option versus the region's main route (the legacy inlet, 0). Drivers pick the cheapest inlet by route cost, so closures shift entry points. Directions follow the regional freeway network (Bay Bridge -> I-80 ramps and the Embarcadero/SoMa grid; US-101/I-280 -> the south edge; western SF -> Market/Mission and the west edge; North Beach/Marin -> Broadway/Columbus and the north edge). Minutes are judgment, not measured.

inlet_class_penalty_min.note: Extra perceived minutes for entering or leaving the map on a lower-class street (slower approach outside the map, more signals). Keeps drivers on arterials unless a closure makes a side street clearly shorter.

through_inlet_max_penalty_min.note: Through-traffic only uses non-freeway inlets whose class penalty is at most this (primary/secondary/tertiary). Freeway-to-freeway traffic stays on the freeway and never enters the street grid. Through volume between map sides is weighted by the lane capacity of each side's eligible inlets.

settle_days_plan.note: replanning days for a plan (warm-started from baseline)

beta_time_per_min.note: typical commute logit time coefficient (MTC/SFCTA range -0.02 to -0.05)

traffic_evaporation_median.note: 62 results, 51 (82%) showed reductions. Median -10.6%, mean -21.9%, central shopping schemes median -13.7%. DENOMINATOR: % of the traffic that previously used the treated road, measured across the wider area - NOT % of total area traffic/VMT. Cairns et al. 1998 report median ~-14%. Validation target, should emerge from behavior.

car_trip_time_elasticity.note: Goodwin 1996: traffic volume w.r.t. travel time ~-0.5 short run, ~-1.0 long run (https://trid.trb.org/View/458127). VTPI lists US urban auto -0.22 (high end of range here).

downtown_sf_worker_mode_share.note: No published work-trip mode split for FiDi-only workplaces was retrievable. Anchors: (1) ACS 2024 B08601, people WORKING in SF County, commuters excl. WFH: drive alone 42.1%, carpool 8.5%, transit 34.2%, walk 8.6%, bike 3.3%, other 3.4%; WFH 15.9% of workers. (2) SFCTA Downtown Travel Study (2023, all trip purposes, downtown): auto 36.9%, transit 20.9%, walk/bike 39.7%, TNC 2.5% (https://www.sfcta.org/sites/default/files/2025-05/Downtown_Travel_Study_FINAL_Report_2025-05-22_Executive_Summary.pdf). FiDi is far more transit-oriented than the county (BART/Muni Metro trunk, $22-40/day parking), so we shift ~16 pts from car to transit/walk. Commute-share values exclude WFH and sum to 1.0; wfh is separate. Sensitivity: use the ACS county split as the car-heavy bound.

car_availability_by_income.note: Anchor: 76.3% of SF-resident workers have >=1 vehicle (B08014: 109,361 of 460,929 have none). No ACS table crosses vehicles by worker earnings; gradient by tier is assumed. Note ACS B08519 (SF workplace) shows auto commute share is nearly flat by earnings (~49% <$15k, ~52% $15-50k, ~50% >=$50k of non-WFH commuters), so income mainly matters through VOT, not car access.

daily_parking_cost_fidi_usd.note: Early bird $22, 12-hr max $40, 24-hr max $46, $8/hr daytime. City garage; private FiDi garages are typically pricier (unverified). Many commuters have employer-paid parking (share unverified).

bart_fare_usd.note: Our computation: ridership-weighted AM fare to Embarcadero/Montgomery: East Bay $6.33 (range $4.20 W. Oakland - $9.95 Berryessa), Peninsula $5.07 (Daly City $4.30 - Millbrae $6.15; SFO $11.80), SF BART $2.55. sf = Muni adult fare $2.85 Clipper/MuniMobile (https://www.sfmta.com/fares). north_bay has no BART: Golden Gate Transit/Ferry fare assumed ~$8 (unverified).

bridge_toll_usd.note: 2026: $8.50 standard, $4.25 carpool weekday peak (FasTrak), westbound only. Primary BATA/MTC source not verified this session (unverified).

walking_speed_m_s.note: 3 mph = 1.34 m/s. MUTCD signal timing uses 3.5 ft/s (1.07 m/s) as a slow-walker design value (https://mutcd.fhwa.dot.gov/htm/2009/part4/part4e.htm).

bike_speed_m_s.note: Urban cycling ~15 km/h incl. signals (common planning assumption; no SF measurement retrieved).

car_free_bike_comfort_bonus.note: perceived-distance discount for cycling on car-free streets; v1 used 0.25 and overshot Market St cycling (+530% vs +25%), revised to the ~10-15% detour cyclists accept for calmer routes

busy_street_bike_penalty.note: perceived-distance factor for cycling on primary/secondary streets with traffic

car_free_walk_comfort_bonus.note: perceived-distance discount for walking on car-free streets; v1 used 0.30 and overshot footfall (+91% vs +29%), revised to the ~10% detour pedestrians accept for pleasant routes

market_pre2020_cost_factor.note: travel-time factor on Market St for private cars before 2020: forced turns at 10th, 6th and 3rd made through-driving impractical (SFMTA 2009/2015 restrictions)

route_noise_sd.note: lognormal sd of perceived edge cost across cyclists (stochastic route choice, 3 draws)

bus_mixed_traffic_share.note: share of Muni's Market St running time exposed to car congestion (red transit-only lanes cover most of Market); v1 used 0.5

sf_office_occupancy_rate.note: SF 47.2% vs 10-city average 55.1%. Measured relative to pre-pandemic swipes in Kastle buildings, not share of all workers. Tue-Thu peaks are higher (unverified daily breakdown).

nonoffice_attendance_rate.note: share of non-office workers present on a weekday

fidi_office_vacancy_rate.note: FiDi 29.0%, South FiDi 24.8%, SoMa 33.2%, citywide 27.2%. CBRE Q1 2026: North FiDi 30.9%, South FiDi 26.1%, SoMa 35.4%, city 30.4% (peak 36.9% Q3 2024) (https://mktgdocs.cbre.com/2299/4b628c03-e0be-422a-af2b-5bd047bb9a65-960261425/San_Francisco_Office_Figures_Q.pdf).

office_sqft_per_job.note: SF Planning employment density factors (office 240). Central SoMa blended ~220. National CBECS median ~600 sqft/worker is not representative of downtown SF (https://www.eia.gov/consumption/commercial/data/2018/bc/pdf/b16.pdf). Multiply by occupancy for on-site workers.

other_sqft_per_job.note: Civic/institutional/PDR density; no SF-specific value retrieved.

sf_persons_per_household.note: ACS 2023 5-yr, tracts in the sim area

visitors_per_day.note: shoppers/tourists entering the area on a weekday

evening_visitors_per_day.note: people coming into the area for dinner/drinks on a weekday evening

lunch_out_share_office_workers.note: 2.6 purchased lunches per in-office week of ~5 days. US national, not SF-specific. Secondary source.

coffee_trip_share.note: 66% daily coffee drinkers x ~29% buying away from home => ~19% of adults/day (derived); bumped for downtown office commuters (assumed).

morning_coffee_share.note: Office workers buying coffee right after arriving; no SF measurement.

avg_ticket_usd.note: cafe $7 ($5-8; SF lattes $6.25-8 unverified), restaurant $28 (Toast full-service lunch check ~$31 per check), fast_food $13 (derived from ezCater $34.82/week over 2.6 lunches), bar $25 (Portland 2012 $17-22/trip inflated, assumed), shop $45 (downtown SF $40-88/visit, 2007-08 survey via Streetsblog). See literature/retail-and-walkability.md.

impulse_capture_per_passerby.note: share of passers-by who stop in (walkers only); calibrated so walkers visit ~2x as often as drivers

huff_distance_decay_per_m.note: Huff/MNL distance decay for walking destination choice

car_free_poi_attractiveness_bonus.note: utility bonus for POIs fronting a car-free street (pleasantness, outdoor seating); v1 used 0.35

walker_vs_driver_visit_ratio.note: Downtown SF: walkers ~8 visits/month vs drivers ~4. Takapuna ~12 vs ~6 is widely cited (https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/handle/10292/999) but its figures could not be retrieved (unverified). Clifton (https://trec.pdx.edu/research/project/411): drivers spend more per trip, walkers/cyclists more per month.

ped_street_retail_uplift.note: Central +15%. NYC Pearl St (FiDi) plaza +14% vs borough; Brooklyn Pearl St +172% (outlier); TfL public-realm upgrades up to +30%; Oslo car-free core ~0 (no harm); Valencia St SF tracked comparison zip; SF parklet businesses +29% vs +10% (Controller 2021, secondary). Volker & Handy (https://ideas.repec.org/a/taf/transr/v41y2021i4p401-431.html): effects positive or non-significant.

ped_footfall_uplift.note: JFK Drive walking +29%, biking +76% (2019-2021). Low = Times Square ped volume +11% (NYC DOT 2010). High = SF Slow Streets walking +65% (SFMTA 2021). Oslo +14% people on street, +43% people staying; Copenhagen car-free area x4 => staying x4.

encounter_window_min.note: CNS Bluetooth scans every 5 min. We use 15-min co-presence bins at places/segments for compute reasons (assumed).

tie_formation_prob_per_repeat_encounter.note: No direct measurement exists. Calibrate so that light-traffic vs heavy-traffic streets reproduce Appleyard's ~2-3x gap in local acquaintances (literature/social-interaction-in-public-space.md). Hall 2019 (https://greatergood.berkeley.edu/article/item/how_long_does_it_take_to_make_a_friend).

repeat_days_per_year.note: Days a habitual lunch-spot pairing repeats per year (hybrid work ~2-3 office days/week).

street_dwell_share_car_free.note: Times/Herald Sq: +84% people staying; Oslo +43% staying. Absolute share lingering is assumed.

slow_street_cost_factor.note: car travel-time factor on a slow street (local access only, barriers; lanes kept). Gives 2nd St about −45% car volume, inside SF Slow Streets' −35…−61%

slow_street_comfort_share.note: share of a car-free street's walking/cycling comfort, lingering and frontage bonus that a slow street gives

appleyard_friends_by_traffic.note: 3.0 vs 0.9 friends confirmed only via Streetfilms transcript; 1.3 moderate (unverified). Acquaintances 'about twice as many' on light streets. Validation target for the social model.

rent_walkability_elasticity.note: Pivo & Fisher: +1% to +9% value per 10 Walk Score points (property type dependent). The engine applies this per 10% change in nearby foot traffic/access - mapping 1 Walk Score point to a 10% foot-traffic change is our assumption. Barcelona green axes: rents +15% within 50 m, +8.5% within 100 m (thesis DiD, case-studies/barcelona-superblocks.md); Seoul Cheonggyecheon land +30-50% within 50 m.

urban_free_flow_speed_kmh.note: TM1 core: freeway 55 mph (88), expressway 40 mph (64), ramp 30 mph (48), major arterial 20 mph (32), collector 10 mph (16). SF default street limit 25 mph (40 km/h). tertiary/residential/living_street are our choices (assumed). Observed congested downtown arterial speed 2025: 12.9 mph AM / 11.5 mph PM (SFCTA CMP 2025, https://www.sfcta.org/reports/congestion-management-program-2025) - use as a validation target, not free flow.

sf_county_worker_mode_share_acs2024.note: Total workers 632,129; WFH 100,347. Computed from table counts (drove alone 224,109; carpool 45,066; transit 181,920; walked 45,522; bike 17,403; taxi+moto+other 17,762).

downtown_trip_mode_share_sfcta.note: All trip purposes, from household travel diaries. Downtown trips -46% within the core 2019-2023; work trips -66%. Downtown workers teleworking 2+ days/week: 14% -> 63%.

persons_per_household_downtown.note: 37,174 residents / 20,604 households. Use for residents of FiDi/SoMa blocks.

soma_office_vacancy_rate.note: Use for SoMa blocks south of Mission.

residential_sqft_per_unit_gross.note: 650 net sqft/unit at 75-80% efficiency => ~850-900 gross; SF '30 by 30' maps 5M sqft -> ~5,000 units (~1,000 gross) (https://sf.gov/reports/july-2024/30-x-30).

walk_detour_factor.note: SF walk network circuity ~1.21 (drive network ~1.31). MATSim default beeline factor 1.3. Only for off-network trips (we route on the graph otherwise).

arrival_time_distribution_sf_workplace.note: n = 531,782. Better than B08302 for downtown inflow timing (includes in-commuters). BART EMBR/MONT exits peak 08:00-08:59 (22-25% of daily exits; data/backend/transit.json).

home_region_share_downtown_workers.note: Excludes home blocks >150 km from FiDi (HQ-reporting artifacts). Unfiltered: east_bay 0.275, peninsula_south_bay 0.179, sf_west 0.092, sf_se_mission 0.119, sf_north 0.040, sf_in_area 0.023, north_bay 0.053, other 0.218. LODES counts jobs at reported worksite (not attendance).

income_tier_share_downtown_workers.note: 322,449 jobs: <= $1,250/mo 21,535; $1,251-3,333/mo 25,892; > $3,333/mo 275,022. Tier 'high' starts at only ~$40k/yr, so split it further with ACS earnings if needed.

muni_speed_change_market_car_free.note: ~6% faster on average; 'up to 12% reduction in Muni travel time' (= +13.6% speed, best line, 9R best). No line-by-line table published. Clean after-window only ~7 weeks before COVID shelter-in-place (Mar 2020). Chronicle: https://www.sfchronicle.com/bayarea/article/Results-of-car-free-Market-Street-so-so-for-SF-15087210.php

parallel_street_max_slowdown_market_car_.note: Worst: Mission St SB 8 AM 10.3 -> 9.9 mph (-4%); worst single hour -6% (Mission SB 9 AM, 5 PM). Adjacent streets average -1% AM / 0% PM; Howard and Folsom got 1-10% faster. INRIX did not report Bush/Pine/Golden Gate/Turk. Only ~200-400 private cars/h used Market peak direction before the ban.

cycling_change_market_car_free.note: Peak-hour bikes ~650 -> >800/h (+25%) 'until Shelter in Place ordered'. https://www.sfmta.com/blog/moving-better-market-street-forward

bay_bridge_aadt.note: Peak hour 15,400. I-80 near 4th/5th St connections 93,000-113,000 AADT. Bay Bridge volume ~9% below pre-pandemic (SFCTA DTS 2025).

downtown_arterial_speed_mph_2025.note: 2019: 10.4 AM / 9.1 PM. Citywide 2025 16.1 / 14.7. Downtown Muni bus 7.1 AM / 6.1 PM. Validation target for baseline congestion.

bart_weekday_exits_downtown_2026_09.note: Values as reported by data-sources agent; data/backend/transit.json gives EMBR exits 20,648 / entries 23,619 from the OD matrix (row/col convention). Sep 2019: EMBR 50,787, MONT 46,263, POWL 25,288 (~41-54% recovery).

cairns_central_shopping_median.note: Median for town-centre / central shopping area schemes (closest analogue to FiDi street pedestrianization).

parking_price_elasticity_vehicle_trips.note: General range -0.1 to -0.3; CBD preferred-parking -0.54 (Hensher & King 2001). SFpark -0.4 is an on-street occupancy elasticity, not mode choice.

mtc_tm1_ivt_coef_work_per_min.note: Non-work -0.0175. Walk <=1.5 mi 2x IVT; transfer = 30 IVT-min; BART IVT weighted 0.8x. Cost coef = 0.6*IVT/VOT.

sfcta_ivt_coef_work_per_min.note: Walk -0.0424, initial wait -0.024. Repo forked from SANDAG ABM3 example; coefficients may not be SF-estimated.
